abstract: Tracks public receptor exposure models, ambient dust vapor suppression, and neighborhood complaints
system_message:
You are the Community Health Assessor (CHA), responsible for tracking public receptor exposure models, ambient dust vapor suppression, and neighborhood complaints, as well as maintaining records from ambient air particulate monitoring.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Ambient air particulate monitoring（AIR）
information_points.content:
CHA-AIR-SST：For Surfactant-enhanced aquifer flushing with reactive barriers, the baseline perimeter PM10 concentration measured at the residential boundary receptor over 24 h is 32 ug/m3.
CHA-AIR-M17：For Ex-situ soil washing with cementitious solidification, the baseline perimeter PM10 concentration at the residential boundary receptor over 24 h is 18 ug/m3.
CHA-AIR-81W：For In-situ thermal desorption with perimeter biosparge, the baseline perimeter PM10 concentration recorded at the residential boundary receptor over 24 h is 24 ug/m3.

information_points.title: Tracks public receptor exposure models, ambient dust vapor suppression, and neighborhood complaints（HEALTH）
information_points.content:
CHA-HEALTH-EAX：For Surfactant-enhanced aquifer flushing with reactive barriers, the neighborhood stakeholder acceptance index is 64 among registered local residents within a 1 km radius of the site perimeter.
CHA-HEALTH-3S3：For Ex-situ soil washing with cementitious solidification, the neighborhood stakeholder acceptance index is 89, based on registered local residents within a 1 km radius of the site perimeter.
CHA-HEALTH-JSS：For In-situ thermal desorption with perimeter biosparge, the neighborhood stakeholder acceptance index is 77, measured among registered local residents within a 1 km radius of the site perimeter.
